sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 34.8% a year from $404.5 million in FY2016 to $5.93 billion in FY2025 [F1][F10][F196].
Growth was front-loaded: 64.2% in FY2021, then 11.8% in FY2022 and 0.1% in FY2023, before recovering to 16.4% in FY2024 and 10.6% in FY2025 [D218][D263][D311][D358][D406].
The FY2017 operating loss of $3.49 billion was driven by a $2.6 billion increase in stock-based compensation, primarily the CEO award and IPO-related RSUs [F12][P74].
The operating margin improved from -422.5% in FY2017 to -9.0% in FY2025, a 5.7pp gain in the latest year alone [F22][F30][D419].
North America remains the largest geography at 58.6% of FY2025 revenue but contributed only 4.4pp of the 10.6% growth [D456][D458][D406].
Other revenue grew 62.9% in FY2025 and contributed 5.4pp, nearly matching advertising's 5.3pp contribution on 5.8% growth [D544][D545][D537][D538].

Advertising growth came from roughly 17% more impressions, largely via Sponsored Snaps and Spotlight, partly offset by a 10% lower cost per impression; other revenue rose on subscription growth [P24].
Operating costs grew 5.1% against 10.6% revenue growth in FY2025, an incremental operating margin of 44.8% [D423][D406][D429].
The diluted share count rose 2.1% in FY2025, so the 35.7% smaller loss per share trailed the 34.0% smaller net loss [D425][D409][D408].
The FY2025 operating margin of -9.0% is the window high, far above the -32.4% median and the -422.5% low [F30][D554][D555][D553].
Cost of revenue fell to 45.0% of revenue from 46.1%, adding 1.1pp to margin, while R&D at 30.2% added 1.3pp [D386][D338][D431][D387][D432].
Sales and marketing fell $42.4 million on timing of marketing events, lower advertising investment and prior-year restructuring charges [P22].
Net margin of -7.8% beat operating margin by 1.2pp, helped by $96.7 million of debt-extinguishment gains in other income [F50][F30][P18].
The margin improvement is real but still leaves the company at the 0th percentile against internet peers, whose median operating margin is 20.3% [D570][D571].
Operating cash flow of $656.2 million and free cash flow of $437.2 million both exceeded the $460.5 million net loss in FY2025 [F80][F100][F40].
Operating cash flow rose on non-cash stock-based compensation of $1.0 billion, D&A of $163.6 million and $96.7 million of debt-extinguishment gains [P13].
Free cash flow margin reached a window high of 7.4%, against a -4.1% median [D393][D560][D561].
Capex was 3.7% of revenue and 1.34x D&A, with purchases mainly for leased-facility improvements [D392][D395][P10].
Net cash swung from $1.44 billion in FY2021 to net debt of $596.3 million in FY2025, the fourth straight year of deterioration [D211][D399][R3].
In February 2025 the company issued $1.50 billion of 2033 Notes and repurchased $1.4 billion of 2026-2028 notes for cash [P2][P1].
Net cash is -10.1% of revenue, at the 0th percentile against internet peers whose median is 45.0% [D400][D578][D579].
Buybacks of $750.9 million were 171.7% of free cash flow in FY2025, and the diluted share count still rose 2.1% [D401][D402][D425].
The company has posted a net loss in each of the last ten years, from $514.6 million in FY2016 to $460.5 million in FY2025 [R1][F31][F40].
Stock-based compensation was 17.1% of revenue in FY2025 and has stayed above 10% for nine straight years [R2][D390][D22].
Net cash has fallen for four consecutive years into net debt, reaching -$596.3 million in FY2025 [R3][D399].
Buybacks exceeded free cash flow in each of FY2023, FY2024 and FY2025, at 544.3%, 142.3% and 171.7% respectively [R4][D307][D354][D402].
Whether the operating margin holds above the FY2025 high of -9.0% or slips back toward the -32.4% median will show if the cost discipline is durable [F30][D554][D555].
Watch net cash against the FY2025 level of -$596.3 million; further decline would extend the four-year slide into net debt [D399][R3].
Watch stock-based compensation against 17.1% of revenue; a move back above the 19.4% FY2024 level would reverse the dilution trend [D390][D342].
